lawyer:
Mr. Abdul Quyum, Advocate ------ For the Petitioner
Mr. Mihir Kanti Majumder with Nahid Yeasmin, Advocates ------ For the Opposite Parties
parties:
Rezaul Karim ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Halima Begum and others ------ Opposite parties
full_judgment:
Syed Amirul Islam, J: This rule arises out of an application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure and is directed against the order No. 123 dated 29.11.1992 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Babugonj, Barisal in Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 1991 allowing the Miscellaneous case under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure (hereinafter referred to as the Code) thereby setting aside the preliminary decree passed on 30.12.1969 and final decree passed on 24.2.81 in Title Suit No. 147 of 1969 of the Court of Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Barisal. 

 The defendant opposite party on 29.8.90 filed Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 1991 in the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Babugonj under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure on the allegations that the summons upon the opposite party was fraudulently suppressed and upon false representation to the court ex-parte decree was obtained and the opposite party claimed to be a resident of village Kayadi and not of Bhramandi at any time and she also claimed that she used to live in different places along with her husband who was a service holder and the opposite party for the first time on 25.9.1991 came to learn about the decree from Abdur Rahim and Abdul Malek and filed the application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code for setting aside the ex-parte decree. 

 3. Mr. Abdul Quiyum, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff petitioner. submits that the learned Assistant Judge have no jurisdiction to entertain an application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code against an ex-parte decree passed by the learned Subordinate Judge who still holds pecuniary and territorial jurisdiction. The learned Advocate further submits that the wording of Order 9 rule 13 does not empower a court to entertain an application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code to set aside the ex parte decree passed by another court and in the instant case the ex-parte decree was passed by the First Court of Subordinate Judge. Barisal and by entertaining the instant Miscellaneous case under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code the learned Assistant Judge. Babugonj in fact sat over the ex-parte decree passed by the First Court of Subordinate Judge which is a superior court and as such the impugned order is a nullity in the eye of law inasmuch as the same has been passed by the learned Assistant Judge without any jurisdiction at all. The learned Advocate further submits that the learned Assistant Judge did not consider that raising of pecuniary jurisdiction of the learned Assistant Judge does not vest him with the power to set aside a decree passed by Subordinate Judge earlier. The learned Advocate further submits that in the instant case the Assistant Judge has no authority in law to sit over the decree passed by the learned Subordinate Judge in Title Suit No. 147 of the 1969 of the Court of Subordinate Judge, Barisal simply on the ground that due to re-orgnisation of courts and raising of the pecuniary jurisdiction the learned Assistant Judge is vested with the same now. The learned Advocate further submits that the instant Miscellaneous case is barred by limitation inasmuch as the ex-parte decree was passed on 30.12.69 and the final decree was passed on 24.2.81 and delivery of possession was given on 17.2.1992 whereas the opposite party No. 1 filed the Miscellaneous case on 10.11.91. The learned Advocate further submits that the case is also, barred by limitation inasmuch as the other defendants who are close relatives of the present opposite party no. 1 have contested the suit after passing of the ex-parte decree and they have lost the case on contest on merit upto the level of the High Court Division. The learned Advocate further submits that even if it is found that the summons was fraudulently suppressed in respect of defendant opposite party No. 1 then also the learned Assistant Judge committed an illegality in re-opening the whole decree by setting aside the entire decree inasmuch as the other defendants contested the decree upto the level of High Court Division and by another defendant upto the Appellate Division and they have lost on merit and the entire decree is set aside and the matter is re-opened those defendants will get benefits indirectly which they could not get directly. 

 4. Mr. Mihir Kanti Majumder, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant opposite party, on the other hand, submits that the service of summons is a question of fact and the trial court on evidence arrived at a finding that no summons was served upon the defendant opposite party and as such rightly arrived at a finding that the ex-parte decree is liable to be set aside. The learned Advocate in this regard relies on the decision reported in 35 D.L.R. (AD) 162 and submits that if it is found that as a matter of fact summons was not served in that case there is no other alternative but to set aside the ex-parte decree and in view of the finding that the summons was not served on the defendant opposite party the learned Assistant Judge rightly set aside the ex-parte decree. Mr. Majumder. in reply to the submission that in the instant case the learned Assistant Judge ought not have set aside the entire decree, submits that it depends on the nature of the case and if the decree is devisible then it will be set aside as against the applicant only otherwise the entire decree will be set aside. The learned Advocate further submits that in view of the nature of the case and for ends of justice the entire decree should be set aside and there is no legal bar for the court to set aside the entire decree on an application of single defendant in a suit for partition between the cognate relatives of the parties and as such the learned trial court rightly set aside the entire decree. Mr. Majumder finally finds it difficult to assail the first submission of by Mr. Quiyum on the point of jurisdiction and candidly submits that if it is found by this court that the learned Assistant Judge has no jurisdiction to entertain the application in that case the impugned order should be set aside and the case should be sent back to the learned Assistant Judge with a direction to dispose of the same in accordance with law. 

 6. In the instant case when Title Suit No. 147 of 1969 was instituted before the Subordinate Judge, Barisal he had the pecuniary and territorial jurisdiction to entertain the suit but after passing of the final decree it appears that due to enhancement of the pecuniary jurisdiction of the Assistant Judges and re-organisation of the territorial jurisdiction both pecuniary and territorial jurisdiction vests in the Court of the Assistant Judge, Babugonj in respect of the property involved in Title Suit No. 147 of 1969. As such now the pertinent question that calls for decision in the instant Rule is as to whether in that view of the matter the learned Assistant Judge has any authority in law to entertain the application filed under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code for setting aside the ex-parte decree passed by the learned Subordinate Judge. First Court, Barisal in Title Suit No. 147 of 1989 

 7. Order 9 rule 13 of the Code declares that an application to set aside the decree may be filed to the court by which the ex-parte decree was passed. It goes on the state that on making an order setting aside the ex parte decree the court shall fix a date for proceeding with a suit. In the instant case the ex parte decree was passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, First Court, Barisal but subsequently there was readjustment of the territorial and pecuniary jurisdiction between that court and the court of Assistant Judge, Babugonj. As a result of which all the properties included in the decree were transferred to the jurisdiction of the court i.e. the Assistant Judge, Babugonj. Subsequently the defendant opposite party No.1 applied to that court to set aside the ex-parte decree passed against him and that court has granted the prayer and the instant revision is against that order and it has been contended by Mr. Quiyum that the learned Sub-ordinate Judge was the only court competent to act under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code to set aside the ex-parte decree and the learned Assistant Judge, Babugonj had no jurisdiction to do so. That rule, it is true, authorise an application to the court which passed the decree but the opposite party in the instant case filed an application before the learned Assistant Judge Babugonj to set aside the same. On a careful scrutiny of the provision of Order 9 rule 13 of the Code it appears that ordinarily the application should be made to the court that passed the decree and not to other court. It does not say anything about other court and the rule does not say that the Court that passed the decree is the only court that can set it aside and there is nothing restrictive in the wording. The expression the court by which the decree was passed" cannot be taken to be limited to the original court as rule 13 of Order 9 is an enabling one which prescribes what is to be done in the ordinary course to get an ex-parte decree set aside. On the formation of new district the properties included in the decree came under the territorial jurisdiction of the court of Assistant Judge, Babugonj. The words used in Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure providing that it should be made to the court by which the decree was passed were not so definite and precise as to exclude the possibility of the application being entertained by the court which has subsequently come to be seized of the jurisdiction. In the instant case admittedly after re-organisation of the districts and enhancement of the pecuniary jurisdiction of the .courts the learned Assistant Judge, Babuganj has jurisdiction to entertain the application under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code. 

 8. Now let me advert to the second submission of Mr. Quiyum. In the instant case, it is contended by Mr. Qauyum, that even if it is found that summons was not served then also the learned Assistant Judge committed an illegality in setting aside the entire decree. The general rule is that on an application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure the court is competent to set aside an ex-parte decree as against the applicant alone but if it is found that the decree in question is indivisible one in that case the Court has no alternative but to set aside the entire decree even though the decree was passed against some of the defendants on contest on merit. It is also well settled that even if the decree is divisible the court in consideration of the nature of the suit and the decree is competent to set aside the decree as a whole for ends of justice. Here it may be mentioned that in the case reported in A.I.R. 1960 (Bom) 485 it has been observed that the wording of the proviso to Order 9 rule 13 provides that where the decree is of such of nature that it cannot be set as die as against one defendant only the decree may be set aside against all or any of the other defendants also. The proviso contemplates cases where the decree is of such a nature that it cannot be set aside against one defendant only in such cases, for instance, a decree for possession of house in the joint possession of persons, a partition decree, and a decree for joint possession of property in the joint possession of two or more persons may be set aside as a whole. The determining factor is the nature of the decree and not the reasons behind the decree. In the instant case the decree in question is a decree in partition suit and it is alleged by the defendant opposite party that she had no knowledge whatsoever about the ex parte decree and admittedly she is a co-sharer in the suit land and at this stage it is difficult to perceive what will be her case in her written statement and what share she would claim in the suit property. In that view of the matter it appears to me that the learned Assistant Judge rightly set aside the entire decree otherwise it could give rise to further legal complications. 

 9. Regarding the submission of Mr. Quiyum that the instant application is time barred as contemplated in Article 164 of the Limitation Act is also without any substance. The question of service of summons is a question of fact which is to be decided on evidence. In the instant case it has been found by the learned Assistant Judge that the defendant opposite party had no knowledge about the ex-parte decree until 25.8.91 and this court sitting in its revisional jurisdiction has no authority to set aside the finding of fact based on materials and evidence on record. True, it is the case of the plaintiff petitioner that the maternal uncle of the defendant opposite party is one of the defendants who contested the decree upto the level of the High Court Division and lost on merit and the sister of the mother of this defendant also con-tested the decree upto the Appellate Division and lost on merit. But that cannot be a ground for throwing the application of the present opposite party if it is found that she had been able to substantiate her case by cogent evidence before the trial court. In this connection it may also be mentioned that once it is found that no summons was served upon the defendant the question of knowledge of the defendant about the pendency of the suit is irrelevant. It is now well settled that when the summons is not duly served on the defendant then the court has no alternative but to set aside the ex-parte decree. In the instant case it has been found by the learned Assistant Judge that the summons of the suit was suppressed and not duly served on the defendant opposite party no. 1 and as such I do not find any reason of interfere with the impugned order.
